summary: Year 2 learners (ages 6-7) find different combinations of real coins that make the same total (e.g. 50p as one 50p, or two 20p + a 10p, or five 10p). The core skill is working SYSTEMATICALLY — starting from the largest coin, or swapping one coin for equivalent smaller ones — and understanding that different coin sets are equal because their VALUES sum to the same total, even though the coins differ. A key constraint: only real denominations exist (there is no 8p coin), but any total can be built from the coins that do exist.
misconceptions: Uses a non-existent coin (e.g. an '8p') to make a total
Finds combinations unsystematically, repeating some and missing others
Tracks the number of coins rather than their total value
Thinks a set with more coins must be worth more, so two ways can't be equal

activities.title: Build a target several ways with a live-updating total
steps: Take a target amount (e.g. 50p) and drag or place real-denomination coins into a tray until they reach the total.
Watch a running total so you can see when the tray reaches exactly 50p.
Once a valid way is found, record it on an organised board or list of 'ways to make 50p', then find another distinct way.
Work from the largest coin first, or swap a coin for equivalent smaller ones, so the search is organised rather than random.
Only real coins are available on the shelf (no 8p), so every solution is one that could really be paid.
activities.insight: Many different coin sets can share the same total value; building each one and watching the total confirm the target makes 'equal value, different coins' directly visible.

activities.title: Swap a coin for equivalent smaller coins without changing the total
steps: Start with one way of making the total (e.g. a single 50p).
Swap one coin for equivalent smaller coins — lift the 50p and replace it with two 20p and a 10p — and check the total is unchanged.
Try other swaps (e.g. 30p made as three 10p; swap to 20p + 10p) and confirm each keeps the same value.
Describe in words why the new set equals the old one: the coin values still sum to the same amount.
activities.insight: Exchanging one coin for equivalent smaller coins keeps the total fixed, so a set with more coins can be worth exactly the same as a set with fewer coins.

activities.title: Sort and match coin sets to totals (recognition practice)
steps: Decide which of several coin sets make a given total (e.g. 'which of these make 50p?').
Sort sets into 'makes 50p' and 'does not make 50p'.
Match a total to a valid coin set.
Spot and reject any set that relies on a non-existent coin, such as an invented 8p.
activities.insight: Checking whether a coin set reaches a stated total, and rejecting sets that use invented coins, reinforces that value is what matters and that only real denominations may be used.

activities.title: Pay a different way — shopkeeper talk (optional spoken extension)
steps: Respond to a shopkeeper asking 'Can you pay 50p a different way?' by naming or laying out another valid coin set.
Explain aloud why the new way is worth the same as the first.
Be challenged to find yet another way, and, when only a few coin types are allowed (e.g. 10p, 20p and 50p), to say how you could be sure you've found them all.
activities.insight: Explaining and justifying equal-value combinations aloud rehearses the reasoning and the language of 'same total, different coins'.

checkQuestion: Set a make-the-total task and WATCH how the child works: (1) 'Show me 50p using these coins. Now make 50p a DIFFERENT way. And another way.' (2) Watch whether they work systematically (largest coin first, or swapping) or at random. (3) 'You made 50p with a 50p coin, and with two 20p and a 10p — why are they the same amount?' Watch for use of real denominations only, an organised approach, and whether they track value.
checkAnswer: Produces several valid combinations for 50p (e.g. 50p; 20p + 20p + 10p; five 10p) using only real coins; works with some system (largest-first or swapping) rather than at random; explains the sets are equal because their values total the same 50p.
